obligation: Nevada Gaming Commission Regulation 5.260 (cybersecurity): all divisions and group
basis: No division holds a gaming license or operates games or wagering

obligation: NIGC MICS, information technology: all divisions and group
basis: No division conducts tribal Class II gaming

obligation: BSA/AML program for casinos: all divisions and group
basis: No division is a casino or card club

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1: Live Venues
applies: Yes (Visa Level 1 merchant; annual QSA ROC and quarterly ASV scans)
basis: Merchant of record for tickets, food and beverage, parking, and merchandise: about 61 million card transactions a year, about 33 million Visa. The acquirer letter of 2026-04-15 requires a QSA ROC by 2026-11-30. The 2025 ROC scope predates the 8 acquired theaters

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1: Hotels and Restaurants
applies: Yes (Visa Level 2 merchant; SAQ D for Merchants with quarterly ASV scans)
basis: Merchant of record for rooms and dining: about 24 million card transactions a year, about 5.4 million Visa. The acquirer letter requires SAQ D by 2026-12-31

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1: Ticketing and Streaming
applies: Yes (service provider ROC, including Appendix A1; streaming merchant)
basis: The TVOP stores, processes, and transmits card data for about 1,150 clients and for the two group merchants, so it is their third-party service provider (Requirements 12.8 and 12.9). Service provider ROC with an AOC dated 2026-03-31, renewal 2027-03-31; the streaming acquirer accepts that ROC for the streaming channel

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1: corporate shared services
applies: Yes (common controls carved into all three validations)
basis: SYS-G1 to SYS-G3 provide controls that the Live Venues ROC, the hotels SAQ D, and the service provider ROC rely on

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Live Venues
basis: Reasonable security and truthful privacy and purchase-limit statements to patrons; no size threshold

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Hotels and Restaurants
basis: Reasonable security for guest card and identity data (FTC v. Wyndham, 3d Cir. 2015) and truthful rate statements

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Ticketing and Streaming and the group
basis: Security and client data statements to clients and patrons, including sales materials on client data use

obligation: FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees: Live Venues
basis: Live-event tickets are a covered good (464.1); venue websites and emails advertise ticket prices

obligation: FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees: Hotels and Restaurants
basis: Short-term lodging is a covered good (464.1); a mandatory $32 resort fee at the 9 venue hotels

obligation: FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees: Ticketing and Streaming
basis: The TVOP renders event and checkout prices for every tenant, so its product design affects the group's and clients' compliance

obligation: ADA Title III ticketing: Live Venues and Ticketing and Streaming
applies: Yes (Live Venues); product duty (Ticketing and Streaming); not applicable (Hotels and Restaurants)
basis: Live Venues sells tickets for places of public accommodation; the pricing and bot modules serve group venues and client tenants. Hotels and Restaurants sells no tickets (ADA lodging rules are outside this analysis)

obligation: BOTS Act: Live Venues and Ticketing and Streaming
basis: Live Venues is a ticket issuer for events in venues with more than 200 seats and the TVOP acts as its agent; bot detection records are evidence. Not applicable to Hotels and Restaurants

obligation: Florida ticket resale and circumvention statute (worked example): Live Venues and Ticketing and Streaming
basis: Civil penalty for circumventing a ticket seller's security measures; Live Venues sells tickets in Florida

obligation: FTC/FACTA Disposal Rule: all divisions and group HR
basis: Group HR and hotel HR offices hold background check reports for workforce screening

obligation: Florida guest register (worked example): Hotels and Restaurants
basis: Hotels in Florida keep a guest register; the PMS keeps it electronically

obligation: State breach notification laws: all divisions
basis: Each division holds personal information of patrons, guests, or subscribers in many states; apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (worked example): all divisions
basis: The group holds personal information of Florida residents; the Ticketing and Streaming division is a third-party agent of its client venues (501.171(6))

obligation: Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act: all divisions
basis: The hotels division collects no biometric identifiers; the face entry pilot runs only at 2 Florida amphitheaters

obligation: Florida Digital Bill of Rights: group
citation: Fla. Stat. ch. 501, part V (controller defined in 501.702)
basis: The group exceeds $1 billion in revenue but meets none of the other controller tests (online advertising revenue, smart speaker service, app store)

obligation: State surveillance-pricing laws (for example Connecticut PA 26-64): Ticketing and Streaming and Live Venues
basis: AI-001 uses no patron-level data; counsel reviews any personalized feature and client deployments in states with such laws

obligation: CIRCIA (proposed): all divisions and group
basis: Final rule not published; reporting is voluntary until a final rule takes effect

obligation: COPPA Rule: all divisions
basis: Ticketing, venue, hotel, and streaming services are general audience; accounts require age 18 or older

obligation: COPPA Rule (amended 2025): Ticketing and Streaming
basis: No child-directed service; accounts require age 18 or older

obligation: CCPA/CPRA and CPPA regulations: group and Ticketing and Streaming
citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq.; Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, 7120-7124
applies: Yes (group as a business; Ticketing and Streaming also a service provider to client businesses)
basis: The group does business in California, exceeds the revenue threshold, and processes personal information of more than 250,000 consumers; the first cybersecurity audit report is due 2028-04-01

obligation: DOJ Data Security Program: all divisions and group
basis: The group holds covered personal identifiers above the bulk threshold; vendor and contractor access must be screened

obligation: Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act (PADFA): group
basis: No division is a data broker; patron data feeds stay inside the group

obligation: FCC CPNI rules: all divisions
basis: No division is a telecommunications carrier

obligation: FedRAMP: Ticketing and Streaming
basis: No federal agency customers; the group holds no federal contracts

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure: group
basis: The holding company is an SEC registrant; divisions contribute incident facts through the group

obligation: Card brand rules and acquirer terms: Live Venues, Hotels and Restaurants, streaming, and the TVOP
citation: Merchant and processing agreements; Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0
basis: Three merchant roles and one service provider role; compromise reporting and investigation duties

obligation: Client agreements: Ticketing and Streaming
basis: Incident notice within 72 hours (24 hours for 186 clients), 99.95% monthly availability, aggregated analytics, PCI DSS acknowledgment, and CCPA service provider terms in the 2024 agreement; 212 clients on pre-2024 terms

obligation: SOC 2 Type 2 commitments: Ticketing and Streaming (ticketing platform)
citation: AICPA Trust Services Criteria; client agreements
applies: Yes (ticketing platform, annually); Live Venues, Hotels and Restaurants, and streaming out of scope
basis: Clients rely on the annual report for Security, Availability, and Confidentiality

obligation: HIPAA Security, Privacy, and Breach Notification Rules: all divisions and group
basis: No division is a HIPAA covered entity or a business associate; the group provides no health care, health plan, or clearinghouse services

obligation: Federal contract cybersecurity and supply chain clauses: all divisions and group
basis: The group holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
